# Level 3 ground mission

Level 2's last fighter starts descent. Blackout creates one ground mission; waking raises the camera from the crash clearing to standing height. Combat waits for **Take control / Resume**. **Skip to crash site** ends only the story. It retains the mission and never clears pilots. Twelve pilots occupy the crash-site route, shuttle patrol and outpost. Kill all pilots, then click **Continue to level 4** for the labelled cockpit transition.

WASD moves relative to camera yaw. Mouse aims when captured; drag the canvas or LOOK pad when capture is denied. F / FIRE shoots in fallback mode. Left/right arrows turn and up/down arrows aim vertically. Fire and all movement/look keys can be remapped; Escape remains the pause key. Space jumps, Shift sprints and R reloads. Escape, lost lock, blur, hidden tab and rotation pause and clear input. Resume never captures the pointer without a click. Touch MOVE, LOOK and action buttons keep separate captured pointers. Opening settings pauses immediately. Resume closes settings and clears held input. Ground settings expose sensitivity, invert Y, FOV, key bindings, graphics, motion, mute and contrast. Reduced motion turns bob off by default.

The pulse blaster has twelve shots and a renewable reload. Energy cells restore magazine shots; health supplies restore health. Ground health starts at 100. A lethal hit consumes one run life, restores health at the crash checkpoint and grants three seconds of immunity. Landing above 12 m/s causes fall damage through the same life/respawn handler; ordinary jumps do not. Defeated pilots and score remain. Zero lives ends the run. Restart starts level 1. No player-name labels appear above pilots.

## Handoff contract

`groundEntryPayload` consumes the reviewed immutable planet visual profile and the frozen terrain world/revision. It retains seed/config, edits, anchor, sun, moons and atmosphere. The actual anchor is `profile.anchor` (currently cell 0,0). The orbital renderer intentionally enlarges terrain cells to 50 cartographic metres; ground uses one authored gameplay metre per cell so a 1.8 metre player can traverse the 160-cell arena. The payload records this explicit `cartographic-cell-preserving` transform: orbital metres / `profile.metresPerBlock` = terrain cell = ground metre. This is a scale transition, not a second seed or regenerated geography. The wreck stands beside that same anchor. Ground collision, navigation, meshes and shots share one snapshot. The reviewed default remains ordinary Canvas descent; experimental orbital rendering stays opt-in. Both paths consume the same pure profile factory. The lab stays locked until restart/Continue. Reviewed descent source is integrated in local base `9b069b275ab4d1d85518366ce969cd1225e64dbd` (PR 63).

`prepareGround` captures once per run. `enterGround` creates at most one mission. Normal waking and repeated Skip use that same payload. Ship velocity, saucers, shield cells and ship projectiles are cleared. Ground completion is latched; score and lives copy back once per update. Continue destroys ground state before level 4. Restart changes run ID and removes mission state. Mesh jobs carry mission ID and revision. Context loss pauses; restored WebGL resources rebuild from CPU state and wait for a Resume click. WebGL failure preserves the run and offers Retry; there is no flat FPS substitute.

The arena spans 160 metres on each horizontal axis, with solid perimeter walls. Planet's protected landing/relay/extraction routes retain their terrain heights. Wreckage, shuttle, outpost and cover use the same absolute coordinates and slab collision as rendering. Terrain materials, including crystals and fungi, are opaque to every shot. Ray DDA plus exact slabs resolve nearest solids; camera aiming also checks muzzle obstruction. Enemy plasma sweeps its travelled segment. Movement substeps at 0.15 metres horizontally and 0.1 metres vertically, within a 60 Hz fixed simulation bounded to six steps. Player collision is a 0.64 metre wide, 1.8 metre high box. Ground step height is 0.55 metres.

Ground meshes remove hidden faces through the full terrain column, including caves and exposed cliffs, in nearby 8×8 chunks. At most one fine chunk and eight coarse distant columns are prepared each frame. The held pulse blaster is a shared 3D voxel mesh, drawn in the same perspective and depth buffer as cover, with muzzle flash, recoil and reload movement. Mesh and shot ray share a pose that follows pitch and pulls the blaster inward for portrait views. Reduced graphics uses a smaller radius and lower pixel ratio. Fine meshes are capped at 121 chunks; total GPU mesh data is limited to 16 MiB. Pilot meshes are shared and their fixed-step positions interpolate for rendering. Actor count is configurable from 1 to 24; default count remains twelve. Plasma, trails, pickups and CPU voxel caching are capped at 32, 12, 16 and 250,000 entries. `WEAPONS.pulse` and `RULES` expose bounded weapon, health, speed, attack, windup and repath settings. Extra actors use deterministic non-overlapping safe positions. Navigation checks continuous clearance, solid feet support and the same step height as movement. Pilots settle under gravity, avoid each other and try a bounded side detour when stuck. Patrol arrival tolerance is smaller than its two-metre route. Blocked goals use at most eight safe-neighbour checks; investigation memory expires after five seconds without sight. Performance must be measured on named hardware; software browser measurements cannot prove the 60 FPS desktop or 30 FPS phone targets.
